title: Regression bridging report - attention engine compatibility checks
summary: Quick synthesis of an investigative run we did to reconcile small but actionable regressions observed after swapping in the new attention kernel and enabling paged-KV + continuous batching. Outcome: functional correctness preserved, but three workload clusters show token-latency shifts and one promptset shows subtle NLG style drift on long-context summarization.
background: Context: onboarding two community models (m-7b-c and m-13b-slim) to the hosted catalog required a runtime reference change: flash-attention v2 kernels + paged KV paging heuristics + continuous batching path enabled. Our standard CI evals passed, but customer smoke tests and nightly eval harness flagged regressions in a small subset of prompt sets (mainly long-context summarization and code-completion with streaming). This doc collects the triangulated evidence, quick hypotheses, and recommended mitigations for rollout decisions.
test_matrix: m-7b-c | flash-attn-v2 enabled | paged-kv=on | cont-batching=on | seq_len=512/2048 | batch=1..8 | promptset=PROMPTSET-1342 (long-summarize)
m-7b-c | flash-attn-v1 (baseline) | paged-kv=off | cont-batching=off | seq_len=512/2048 | batch=1..8 | promptset=PROMPTSET-1342
m-13b-slim | flash-attn-v2 | paged-kv=on | cont-batching=on | seq_len=1024/4096 | batch=1..4 | promptset=CODE-COMP-089 (streaming code)
Stress runs: synthetic prefix reuse workload (KV hit rate 0.6 / 0.9) | perf traces + KV miss amplification
Regression smoke: end-to-end throughput/latency and functional checks (exact match tokens, perplexity on held-out evals, and BLEU/ROUGE for summarization)
eval_results: Latency: p50 token latency increased by +4.5ms on m-7b-c at seq_len=2048 when cont-batching=on + paged-kv=on compared to baseline; p95 unchanged for seq_len=512.

Throughput: batching gives expected token/s gains for short contexts, but with paged-KV enabled we see throughput variance when cache eviction occurs (spikes observed at ~11:22 UTC during mixed workload).

Quality: summarization ROUGE-L dropped 1.8 points on PROMPTSET-1342 (long-context) — behavior change is stylistic (more conservative sentence compression), not hallucination increase by our measures but external reviewer flagged utility drop).
Streaming/code: small increase in stream-chunk delay (avg +22ms per chunk) on CODE-COMP-089 with cont-batching; causes more visible inter-token pauses in clients that render per-chunk.
Functional correctness: logits diffs show rare token flips (<0.03% tokens) concentrated at sequence boundaries where paged-KV page transitions happened.
diff_highlights: Token-level diff heatmap correlates with paged-KV boundary events (page flushes at ~512-token multiples).
Flash-attention v2 micro-ops did not change final logits distribution significantly by L2, but numerical ordering of near-equal logits created downstream top-1 swaps for ambiguous tokens.
Continuous batching introduces small extra queuing latency for early-response tokens in streaming mode — visible as increased jitter in per-token arrival time despite similar aggregate throughput.
One prompt in PROMPTSET-1342 shows consistent truncation of secondary clause (style shift) across both m-7b-c and m-13b-slim when run with page size=512 and cont-batching enabled.
regression_hypotheses: Numeric instability at page boundary: paged-KV page flush causes subtle differences in KV cache ordering combined with float reductions in flash-attn-v2 creating token ranking flips.
Batch routing changes: continuous batching merges early short requests which delays immediate emission; some client-facing metrics treat this as increased latency.
Model sensitivity: long-context summarization promptset contains brittle templates that prefer older tokenization edge-cases; minor logit perturbations change compression choices.
Telemetry sampling gap: our nightly evals rarely hit the exact KV hit/miss patterns that occur in production mixed workloads — we under-sampled boundary cases.
root_cause_analysis: Synthesis points to a confluence: paged-KV introduces discrete boundary events that interact with the new flash-attention execution order (reduced internal eps/accumulation differences). These cause low-probability top-1 swaps at sequence boundaries. Continuous batching amplifies client-perceived latency for early tokens because of batching aggregation time plus page-load pauses. No evidence of a correctness bug in attention math; instead, numerical ordering + caching policy yields observable diffs in a targeted subset of prompts.
recommended_actions: Rollback not required for general rollout — problem isolated to long-context summarization + streaming code workloads.

Short-term mitigations: 1) for hosted catalog, disable continuous batching for streaming-enabled routes for affected models; 2) increase page size to 1024 for summarization routes to reduce boundary frequency; 3) add a jitter-reduction patch to batching router to prioritize low-latency small requests.
Mid-term: upstream patch in flash-attn-v2 to standardize reduction order (PR linked in artifacts) and add deterministic accumulation path behind a feature flag for sensitive routes.
Eval improvements: expand nightly eval harness to include synthetic KV-boundary workloads and add PROMPTSET-1342 variant with slightly altered tokenization to cover brittle templates.
Monitoring: add a specific alert for sudden ROUGE/L doc-level drops on long-context routes and a token-diff sampler for page-boundary events.
